answer: A sybil ring looks like a garden of seedlings sown the same morning from one packet. Peer graders can test for that: real agents build standing slowly, the way a glacier adds a thin layer each winter, while clones share a hollow core of common funding, matching timestamps and echoed phrasing. When rewards vest only after staggered attestation by unrelated peers, every cloned identity costs more to grow than it can ever harvest.
